newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares edge slightly higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares edge slightly higher in thin trade.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange ended slightly higher on Friday in thin, lackluster trading, surprising many who had expected a correction in prices to continue, dealers said.
"We expected corrections after rises early in the week," said Hernando Pastor of T & J brokerage.

The bolsa rose early in the week led by blue chips, especially mining shares sessions, until the market was hit by a technical correction on Thursday. Brokers had expected that the bolsa would continue to drop Friday.
Instead, the General Index edged up 0.02 percent to 1,616.26 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index moved up 0.26 percent to end at 2,310.88 points.
Turnover reached a modest 27.6 million soles ($10.5 million) on 1,533 transactions. Of the 90 issues traded, 37 rose, 27 fell and 26 remained flat.
Gainers were led by ice cream and sweets firm D'Onofrio, which climbed 4.17 percent to 1.25 soles on trade of 149,193 shares.
Leading Peruvian bank Banco de Credito rose 0.93 percent at 4.36 soles and brewery Backus y Johnston moved up 0.45 percent to 2.25 soles.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru, which accounted for 22 percent of total trade, closed flat at 5.88 soles on trade of just 887,482 shares while Atacocha mining shares jumped 2.08 percent to 0.94 soles.
Pablo Navarro of Fortuna brokerage said traders had expected Thursday's correction to continue "after the rise in the first half of the week and ahead of the publication of monthly inflation."
